newsitem.title: USA: Seitel Wharton, Texas gas well complete.
newsitem.headline: Seitel Wharton, Texas gas well complete.

text.p: Parallel Petroleum Corp said Tuesday a natural gas well in Wharton County, Texas near the gulf coast had been completed.
It said the Cox & Perkins Lange No. 2 well, the 13th to be completed in the Yegua formation, had a calculated open flow potential of 30.2 million cubic feet per day.
DDD Energy Inc, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Seitel Inc, has a 50-percent interest in the well.
On a 10/64-inch choke, the well flowed at a rate of 2.1 million cubic feet of gas and 180 barrels of condensate per day, it said.
Parallel Petroleum, which owns a 20-percent working interest in the well, said flowing tubing pressure was 5,262 pounds per square inch, with final shut-in pressure of 5,367 per square inch.
Cox & Perkins has a 10-percent working interest in the well, while Tenneco Venture of Tenneco Inc has 10 percent and individual investors own the remaining 10 percent.
Parallel Petroleum said tests were made from selective perforations from 9,369 feet to 9,405 feet below ground.

It said the operator of the well, Cox & Perkins Exploration Inc., planned to gradually increase production to a stabilized rate of about 5.0 million cubic feet of gas and 450 barrels of condensate per day.
Sales from the well began August 22, it added.
Based on that rate and current market prices for the fuel, the company said it expected net cash flow to its interest would be about $100,000 per month.
Parallel Petroleum said six additional wells have been scheduled to be drilled in the Yegua/Frio gas trend in 1996 -- three in the Frio and three in the deeper, more prolific Yegua formation.
